_readme: Official court and justice-ministry sources, one block per jurisdiction.
These are primary sources: a judgment handed down by a court and a notice
published by a ministry are public acts, and in most of these jurisdictions
they are expressly outside copyright or released under an open licence.
That is the whole reason this pillar exists — it is the one body of legal
information a directory can build on without depending on Chambers, Legal
500 or Law.asia, none of whom own a word of it.
`status` starts as 'unverified' for every entry. fetch_court_records.py
probes each one, records what actually came back, and rewrites the status.
Nothing here is treated as working because it looks plausible — the first
firm crawl taught that lesson expensively.
`licence` is recorded per source because it varies enormously and governs
what we may republish. UK Find Case Law is Open Justice Licence. Korean and
Japanese government works are free of copyright by statute. Some judgment
databases permit reading but not bulk redistribution, and those are marked
'headline-and-link' — we publish the citation and link out, nothing more.
Judgment full text is NEVER republished. The site shows case name, court,
date, citation and a link to the official record. That is a fact set, it is
what a reader needs, and it keeps us clear of every database right.
